items.headline: China market regulator urges 9 e-commerce platforms to tighten quality controls; Alibaba's Hong Kong shares close down 6.2%
items.summary: SAMR's Oct 21 notice (counterfeits, mismatched descriptions, false advertising) hit Alibaba's HK shares, which closed at HK$97.30 (-6.17%), the steepest drop in about two months. The US ADR closed Oct 21 at $104.41 (-3.87%) and traded near $99.60 premarket Oct 22; its Oct 22 close was not verified. Regulatory scrutiny can raise compliance costs and pressure the multiple.

driver.text: US futures are slightly lower after Thursday's AI-funding rout (SOX -6.7%, Nasdaq -2.6%, with all 30 SOX members down). Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said there is 'a scarcity of capital' for AI infrastructure and neoclouds lack working capital, which is weighing on chips; Nvidia is up about 0.4% premarket after closing -4.4%. Oil is firm (Brent about $114, WTI above $101) on reports the US and Israel may consider new strikes on Iran after the November midterms. The 10Y yield fell 17 bp to 4.96% on Thursday (largest one-day drop since March 2023); a 4.98% reading was quoted at 6:19 AM ET.

items.headline: Tesla closes -3.1% at $374.58 after capex cut and thin margins
items.summary: Q3 revenue was flat near $28.0B; adjusted EPS $0.48 beat the ~$0.45 estimate but GAAP EPS fell to $0.22 and operating margin was 2.6% vs 5.8% a year ago. Full-year 2026 capex guidance was cut to about $20B from more than $25B. Rising operating expenses until products like Optimus commercialize remain the focus.
